name: Bathroom & Sanitary
tagline: Sanitaryware, brassware and the plumbing decisions behind them
description: Bathrooms are decided at first fix and judged at handover. Wall-hung fixtures need a concealed cistern in the wall; a rain shower needs pressure the building may not have. Every item here lists what the plumbing has to provide, not just the finish.

materials.name: Floor-mounted WC
materials.blurb: Standard one-piece or two-piece pan on the floor
materials.description: The straightforward specification: no wall carrier, no concealed cistern, easy to service. One-piece models look cleaner and cost more; two-piece are easier to move up a staircase.

specs.Trap: S-trap or P-trap — confirm on site

materials.name: Wall-hung WC
materials.blurb: Floating pan on a concealed carrier — the floor cleans under it
materials.description: The cistern and frame sit inside the wall, leaving the pan floating clear of the floor. Visually far lighter and much easier to clean, but the wall must be built to take the carrier from the start.

materials.name: Counter-top basin
materials.blurb: Bowl that sits proud on the vanity — a design object
materials.description: Ceramic, stone or glass bowls resting on the counter. They demand a taller tap or a wall-mounted spout, and a counter height reduced to around 750 mm so the rim lands correctly.

materials.name: Under-counter basin
materials.blurb: Bowl fixed beneath the counter for a seamless top
materials.description: The counter runs unbroken over the bowl, which makes wiping the surface effortless. Requires a stone or solid-surface top cut and polished at the rim.

materials.name: Wall-hung wash basin
materials.blurb: Basin on brackets or a concealed carrier, no vanity below
materials.description: The lightest-looking option and the best for a very small bathroom or a wheelchair-accessible one. No storage, so plan a mirror cabinet or niche nearby.

specs.Waste: Bottle trap visible — specify a finished one

materials.name: Basin faucet
materials.description: The most-touched piece of brassware in the house. Match the spout projection to the basin — too short and water hits the rim, too long and it splashes out of the bowl.

materials.name: Overhead shower
materials.blurb: Fixed head on an arm — the everyday shower
materials.description: Simple, reliable and pressure-tolerant. A 100–150 mm head with a good spray pattern outperforms an oversized rain head on the low pressure most Indian apartments actually have.

materials.name: Rain shower
materials.blurb: Large ceiling head that needs real pressure to deliver
materials.description: A 200–400 mm head, usually ceiling-mounted, giving a soft drenching flow. Check the head's minimum bar rating against the building's supply — a rain shower on weak pressure just dribbles.

materials.name: Hand shower
materials.blurb: Handheld spray on a hose and rail or wall hook
materials.description: Essential in Indian bathrooms for cleaning the enclosure, bathing children and washing the floor. Always specify it alongside a fixed head, never instead of one.

materials.name: Concealed diverter
materials.blurb: In-wall valve that switches between shower outlets
materials.description: The body is buried in the wall with only the handle and plate visible. Order it early — the concealed part must be installed before tiling, and it is the most common cause of a delayed bathroom.

specs.Brand match: Keep body and trim same brand

materials.name: Bathtub
materials.blurb: Freestanding, drop-in or built-in soaking tub
materials.description: Confirm three things before specifying: the slab loading with the tub full, the hot-water capacity to fill it, and whether it will physically pass through the door.

materials.name: Shower enclosure
materials.blurb: Toughened glass screen that keeps the rest of the room dry
materials.description: From a single fixed panel to a full sliding cubicle, always in 8–10 mm toughened glass. A properly sloped floor and a shower profile matter more than the glass thickness.

materials.name: Floor drain / trap
materials.blurb: The detail that decides whether a bathroom smells
materials.description: A deep-seal anti-odour trap with a removable hair catcher, sized to clear the shower flow. Cheap to specify, expensive to correct once the floor is tiled.

materials.name: Bathroom accessories set
materials.blurb: Towel rails, robe hooks, paper holders, grab bars
materials.description: The small brassware that has to match the taps and be fixed into something solid. Mark every position on the tiling drawing so the fixings do not land on a joint.

specs.Fixing: Into solid backing, not hollow tile

materials.name: Bathroom mirror
materials.blurb: Plain, backlit or demisting mirror over the basin
materials.description: Backlighting flatters and a demister keeps it usable after a shower — both need a fused spur behind the mirror, which must be planned before tiling.

materials.name: Bathroom vanity
materials.blurb: Storage under the basin, built to survive a wet room
materials.description: The one piece of joinery permanently exposed to water — so the carcass should be WPC or marine ply, never MDF. Wall-hung vanities keep the floor clear and dry.
